evidence.note: The official launch disclosure establishes high API prices and describes compute intensity. It does not establish internal costs, losses, or financial ruin.
The contemporary price comparison establishes 30-fold input and 15-fold output prices relative to GPT-4o. Its capability characterization is commentary rather than an independent measurement.

Company-reported science and mathematics gains challenge a blanket characterization of limited improvements. The same table supports deficits against o3-mini on three benchmarks; neither finding establishes overall everyday usefulness.
The independent evaluation concerns an earlier checkpoint and limited autonomy tasks. It provides relevant context but does not directly measure the released model's overall improvement.

reviews.rationale: The confidence-qualified compound claim is not scoreable under the policy. Higher customer prices are established, while the benchmark evidence contains both substantial gains and comparative deficits. These findings do not justify stripping the hedge.

attribution.note: Zitron directly asserts the necessity of expansion.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves an absolute necessity claim. The surrounding discussion identifies data center expansion as its subject.

contract.note: Continued industry capability and deployment growth requiring physical capacity expansion is an ordinary contextual reading. The industry scope and sustained-growth interpretation affect what would count as a counterexample.

evidence.note: The research demonstrates capability gains at the same training-compute budget and reduced downstream compute needs. It does not establish sustained deployment growth within an unchanged physical capacity footprint.
The IEA projects electricity consumption under demand and efficiency assumptions. Consumption forecasts do not establish the causal necessity of additional installed capacity.

reviews.rationale: Efficiency research challenges a simple link between progress and more infrastructure, while projected demand indicates infrastructure pressure. Neither establishes or refutes necessity through matched capability, deployment, and physical-capacity evidence.
